name: Vendor Evaluation
description: Evaluate vendors against requirements, evidence, total cost, security/privacy, implementation risk, support, and exit strategy without letting demos choose the winner by hypnosis.

tasks.name: Define decision requirements
tasks.objective: Define use cases, must-haves, weighted tradeoffs, volumes, integrations, data/security/privacy constraints, service requirements, implementation capacity, budget, and exit requirements before seeing vendor scores.

tasks.name: Build candidate set
tasks.objective: Identify viable vendors and credible build/status-quo alternatives from independent research and stakeholder input; record exclusions and avoid pay-to-play rankings as primary evidence.

tasks.name: Collect comparable evidence
tasks.objective: Request standardized responses, pricing, architecture, security/privacy documentation, SLAs, support model, references, roadmap dependencies, implementation assumptions, and contract terms. Normalize units and missing answers.

tasks.name: Run proof-of-value scenarios
tasks.objective: Test the same representative workflows and edge cases with each shortlisted option using realistic data/volumes where safe. Capture setup effort, failures, latency, usability, integration friction, and support response.

tasks.name: Model total cost and risk
tasks.objective: Estimate licenses/usage, implementation, migration, operations, training, support, lock-in, switching, downtime, security/privacy exposure, roadmap dependence, and plausible growth scenarios.

tasks.name: Verify claims independently
tasks.objective: Check references, incident/status history, public filings/docs, contract language, certifications and audit scope, support claims, and customer experiences relevant to the target use case. Treat badges as scoped evidence, not universal safety proof.

tasks.name: Publish decision record
tasks.objective: Present requirements compliance, proof results, costs, risks, unknowns, contract blockers, implementation and exit plans, and sensitivity to assumptions. Preserve tradeoffs rather than hiding them behind a single vendor score.
